To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the separation of H2 and its isotope D2 in the temperature range of 27-207 K has been studied using a specially designed surface acoustic wave sensor with a very short response time, (b) the sensor chip has been modified by the growth of an ultramicroporous metal-organic framework (MOF) with a very narrow pore size of 2.6 Å, (c) a quantum sieving behavior has been found in this temperature range,
a metal-organic-framework grown on a sensor chip can be used for the on-chip dynamic study of the kinetic H2 /D _{2} quantum sieving.

the quantum sieving effect in the metal-organic framework MFU-4 can be observed in the temperature range between 27 K and 207 K, with D2 having a higher diffusion coefficient than H2 below the critical temperature of 64 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel sensor chip with a very fast and sensitive response for gas flow measurements in the temperature range from 27 K to room temperature, which is based on surface acoustic wave (SAW).
the separation of H _{2} /D _{2} using quantum sieving on MOF MFU-4.
the development of new materials and their application in the separation of hydrogen isotopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantum sieving effect is observed in the studied system.
the quantum sieving effect is observed for H2 and D 2 in the narrow pores of MFU-4 in the temperature range of 27-64 K.
the H2 /D _{2} selectivity of MOFs is determined by the size of the pores, the strength of the interaction of the gas molecules with the framework and the temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum sieving effect of H2 /D _{2} in MOF materials is a function of temperature and the pore size of the MOF.
the quantum sieving effect of H2 /D 2 is observed for the first time in an ultramicroporous metal-organic framework, which is confirmed by the molecular dynamics simulations.
the quantum sieving effect is a result of the combination of the ultra-narrow pore and the flexible framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MOFs can be successfully used for H2 /D _{2} separation at room temperature and below.

the use of a sensor chip allows us to measure the dynamic behavior of the gas diffusion process in a MOF and to determine the diffusion coefficients of H2 and deuterium in the temperature range of interest.
MOFs can be used for the selective separation of H2 and/or D2, depending on the temperature.
